Replacing SwingX in mystic-crypt-ui (org.swinglabs.swingx:swingx-all 1.6.5-1, LGPL)

SwingX is licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1 or (at your
option) any later version (COPYING, lgpl-2.1.txt and JXLabel-header.txt in this directory).
mystic-crypt-ui is licensed under the MIT License and uses SwingX as a library. You may
replace SwingX by a modified version of it, and modify the application for your own use,
including reverse engineering for debugging such modifications, as section 6 of LGPL-2.1
requires of a work that uses the library.

The application jar (mystic-crypt-ui.jar in the installation directory) is one jar that
holds the classes of SwingX unpacked: those of the packages org.jdesktop.swingx and
org.jdesktop.beans, and its service file META-INF/services/
org.jdesktop.swingx.plaf.LookAndFeelAddons.

1. Get the sources of the version the application was built with:
   https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/swinglabs/swingx/swingx-all/1.6.5-1/swingx-all-1.6.5-1-sources.jar
   (the jar of the same version: .../swingx-all-1.6.5-1.jar). Change it as you wish and
   build your own jar from it, as interface-compatible with 1.6.5-1 as the application needs.
2. Start the application with your jar in front of the application jar on the class path,
   so that the JVM loads the classes of SwingX from yours:

   java --add-opens java.base/java.time=ALL-UNNAMED \
        --sun-misc-unsafe-memory-access=allow \
        --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED \
        -cp my-swingx-all.jar:mystic-crypt-ui.jar \
        io.github.astrapi69.mystic.crypt.StartMysticCryptApplication

   The first two options are those start.sh starts the application with; the third is
   the one the jar's manifest sets only for java -jar, which -cp does not read. On
   Windows use javaw with the same options and ; as the class path separator:

   javaw --add-opens java.base/java.time=ALL-UNNAMED --sun-misc-unsafe-memory-access=allow --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED -cp my-swingx-all.jar;mystic-crypt-ui.jar io.github.astrapi69.mystic.crypt.StartMysticCryptApplication

   This command has not been run; check it against your installation.
   The application jar is not changed by this, and a modified SwingX takes the place of
   the shipped one.
3. Alternatively unpack the application jar, replace the files of the packages named above
   by those of your build, and pack the jar again; the signature of the original jar is
   then no longer valid, which the LGPL leaves to you.

The source of the application itself, for relinking, is at
https://github.com/astrapi69/mystic-crypt-ui (MIT License).
